extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and PTO officials
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory and procedural criteria governing filing requirements (oath/declaration/substitute statements/assignments), citation and preissuance submissions, reexamination/inter partes/post-grant review proceedings, evidentiary standards, amendments, estoppel, damages (reasonable royalty and willfulness), and the composition/duties of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement under this subsection shall identify the individual with respect to whom the statement applies; set forth the circumstances representing the permitted basis for the filing of the substitute statement in lieu of the oath or declaration under subsection (a); and contain any additional information, including any showing, required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the three content elements that must be present in a substitute statement and that the Director may require further showings or information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making required statements in assignment of record
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who is under an obligation of assignment of an application for patent may include the required statements under subsections (b) and (c) in the assignment executed by the individual, in lieu of filing such statements separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits inclusion of required inventor statements inside assignment documents instead of separate filings; affects recordation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing oath/declaration or substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of allowance under section 151 may be provided to an applicant for patent only if the applicant has filed each required oath or declaration under subsection (a) or has filed a substitute statement under subsection (d) or recorded an assignment meeting the requirements of subsection (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions issuance of notice of allowance on having inventor oath/declaration, substitute statement, or qualifying recorded assignment on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier-filed application exemption for required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements do not apply to an individual with respect to an application that claims the benefit of an earlier filing date under section 120 or 365(c) if an oath/declaration, substitute statement, or qualifying assignment meeting requirements was executed and filed or recorded in connection with the earlier-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If qualifying statements/assignments exist in an earlier-filed application, the duty to refile them in the later application is waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental and corrected statements; remedy for failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person making a statement required under this section may withdraw, replace, or otherwise correct the statement at any time. If a change requires filing additional statements, such statements shall be filed according to regulations. No patent shall be invalid or unenforceable based upon failure to comply with a requirement under this section if the failure is remedied as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows correction and supplementation of required statements and provides a savings clause preventing invalidation if remedied as allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of penalties in declarations/statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any declaration or statement filed under this section must contain an acknowledgment that any willful false statement is punishable by fine or imprisonment, or both, under section 1001 of title 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires an express criminal-penalty acknowledgment to be included in inventor oaths, declarations, or substitute statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by other than inventor — proprietary interest and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign the invention may make an application for patent. A person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest may make an application on behalf of and as agent for the inventor on proof of the pertinent facts and a showing that such action is appropriate to preserve the rights of the parties. If the Director grants a patent on such an application, the patent shall be granted to the real party in interest and upon such notice to the inventor as the Director considers sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who may file an application when not the inventor, the proof required, and that the patent is issued to the real party in interest with notice to inventor as determined by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and claim drafting subsection labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification paragraphs are renumbered as subsections (a) In General, (b) Conclusion, (c) Form, (d) Reference in Dependent Forms, (e) Reference in Multiple Dependent Form, and (f) Element in Claim for a Combination, with corresponding changes in textual references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural/formatting changes that clarify subsection headings and the labeling of claim-related provisions; impacts how specification text and claim rules are cited and applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable royalty — court to select framework and identify relevant factors
rubrics_metrics.description: An award based upon a reasonable royalty shall be determined in accordance with this subsection. Based on the facts of the case, the court shall determine whether paragraph (2), (3), or (5) will be used by the court or the jury in calculating a reasonable royalty. The court shall identify the factors that are relevant to the determination of a reasonable royalty under the applicable paragraph, and the court or jury shall consider only those factors in making the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires the court to choose among specifically described analytical approaches and to identify and limit consideration to relevant factors for the chosen approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment — relate damages to patent's contribution over prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall conduct an analysis to ensure that a reasonable royalty is applied only to that economic value properly attributable to the patent’s specific contribution over the prior art, excluding economic value properly attributable to the prior art and other features or improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes an apportionment requirement to exclude value derived from prior art or other features when computing reasonable royalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire market value rule limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the claimant shows that the patent’s specific contribution over the prior art is the predominant basis for market demand for an infringing product or process, damages may not be based upon the entire market value of the products or processes involved that satisfy that demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents using the entire market value of a multi-component product unless the patented feature drives consumer demand (predominant basis test).

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation for combination inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For combination inventions the patentee may show that the contribution over the prior art may include the value of the additional function resulting from the combination, as well as the enhanced value, if any, of some or all of the prior art elements resulting from the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows patentees of combination inventions to capture value of emergent functions and enhanced value of combined elements, while still subject to apportionment over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other factors for determining reasonable royalty
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining a reasonable royalty, the court may also consider, or direct the jury to consider, the terms of any nonexclusive marketplace licensing of the invention, where appropriate, as well as any other relevant factors under applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits consideration of marketplace licensing evidence and other relevant legal factors alongside apportionment and market demand analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased damages for willful infringement and required proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A court that has determined that the infringer has willfully infringed may increase the damages up to three times the amount of damages found or assessed under subsection (a). A court may find willful infringement only if the patent owner presents clear and convincing evidence that (A) after receiving written notice from the patentee alleging acts of infringement with particularity and identifying each claim and accused product/process, the infringer, after reasonable opportunity to investigate, thereafter performed one or more of the alleged acts; (B) the infringer intentionally copied the patented invention with knowledge it was patented; or (C) after being found by a court to have infringed, the infringer engaged in conduct not colorably different and resulted in a separate finding of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a heightened standard (clear and convincing evidence) and specifies permitted grounds for finding willfulness, including a particularized pre-suit notice requirement as one route to willfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on willfulness due to informed good faith belief
rubrics_metrics.description: A court may not find that an infringer has willfully infringed for any period during which the infringer had an informed good faith belief that the patent was invalid or unenforceable, or would not be infringed by the conduct later shown to constitute infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an affirmative defense period for an infringer who had an informed, good-faith belief as to invalidity/non-infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence establishing informed good faith belief
rubrics_metrics.description: An informed good faith belief may be established by reasonable reliance on advice of counsel; evidence that the infringer sought to modify its conduct to avoid infringement once it discovered the patent; or other evidence a court may find sufficient. The decision not to present evidence of advice of counsel is not relevant to willfulness determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists non-exhaustive examples of evidence that can establish an informed good-faith belief and states that silence on advice-of-counsel is not an adverse inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on pleading and bench determination of willfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the date on which a court determines that the patent is not invalid, is enforceable, and has been infringed, a patentee may not plead and a court may not determine that an infringer has willfully infringed. The court’s determination of willfulness shall be made without a jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precludes early pleading of willfulness before a final determination of validity/enforceability/infringement and requires judge (not jury) for willfulness determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier-inventor / commercial use defense standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends defenses to require that the subject matter was commercially used, or that the party made substantial preparations for commercial use, before the effective filing date of the claimed invention for qualifying as a defense under section 273.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts earlier-inventor defenses toward activity and commercial-use/substantial-preparation standards prior to the effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory periodic review of amendments effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than the end of the 7-year period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, and every 7 years thereafter, the Director shall conduct a study on the effectiveness and efficiency of the amendments made by this section and submit a report including recommendations to the Judiciary Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates regular, periodic evaluation and reporting by the PTO Director of the impact of statutory amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of prior art by any person and inclusion in official file
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may cite to the Office in writing prior art consisting of patents or printed publications or written statements of the patent owner filed in proceedings, and if the person explains the pertinence and manner of applying the prior art to at least one claim, the citation and explanation shall become part of the official file of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opens the file to third-party submissions of prior art and owner statements provided the submitter explains relevance to at least one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and limitations for written statements submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: A party submitting written statements shall include any other documents, pleadings, or evidence from the proceeding that address the patent owner’s statements or the claims; such statements shall not be considered for any purpose other than to determine the proper meaning of the claims that are the subject of a request in a proceeding ordered pursuant to section 304 or 313; materials subject to a protective order shall be redacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the use of submitted written statements to claim-construction purposes in specified proceedings and requires inclusion of related materials and redaction where subject to protective orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity-withheld option for third-party citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the written request of the person citing prior art or written statements, the person’s identity shall be excluded from the patent file and kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows anonymous submission of prior art/written statements to the Office on written request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination — Director determination of substantial new question within three months
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months after the owner of a patent files a request for reexamination, the Director shall determine whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim is raised by the request, with or without consideration of other patents or printed publications. The existence of a substantial new question is not precluded by prior citation or consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a three-month gatekeeping timeframe for Director to decide whether reexamination is warranted and clarifies that prior citation does not bar finding a substantial new question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes proceedings — APJ hearing, comment timing, and oral hearing right
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination proceedings shall be heard by an administrative patent judge in accordance with procedures the Director shall establish; third-party requester shall have opportunity to file written comments on any Office action or patent owner response if received within 60 days after service; at the request of a third party or the patent owner, the administrative patent judge shall conduct an oral hearing unless cause lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies adjudicative forum (APJ), deadlines for third-party comments, and availability of oral hearings subject to judge's finding of cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel narrowed (striking 'or could have raised')
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 315(c) is amended by striking 'or could have raised', narrowing the scope of estoppel arising from certain proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduces the breadth of estoppel so that it may no longer preclude arguments that a party 'could have raised' in earlier proceedings; focuses estoppel on what was actually raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on reexamination after district court judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the judgment of the district court has been entered, reexamination (or certain post-grant administrative review) is prohibited regarding issues resolved by that judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents duplicative administrative reexamination after a final district court judgment on the same issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review — who may file and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the patent owner may file a petition for cancellation seeking to institute a post-grant review proceeding to cancel as unpatentable any claim of a patent on any ground that could be raised under paragraphs (2) or (3) of section 282(b). The Director shall establish fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits petitioners to non-owners and allows challenges on statutory invalidity grounds; requires fee-setting by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review timing — 12-month window or owner consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant proceeding may be instituted only if the petition is filed not later than 12 months after the grant of the patent or issuance of a reissue patent, or if the patent owner consents in writing to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a 12-month statutory window after grant for filing post-grant review petitions unless owner agrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of petition for post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: A cancellation petition must be accompanied by payment of the fee, identify the cancellation petitioner, set forth in writing the basis for the cancellation identifying each claim challenged and provide such information as the Director may require, and include copies of patents and printed publications relied upon; the petitioner must provide copies to the patent owner or designated representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies content, fee, evidence copy, and service obligations for post-grant petitions, and gives the Director regulatory authority to require additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited duplicate filings in post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review proceeding may not be instituted if the petition identifies the same cancellation petitioner and the same patent as a previous petition filed under that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents repetitive petitions by the same petitioner on the same patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's gatekeeping and nonreviewable institution decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall determine if the petition and evidence establish a substantial question of patentability for at least one claim and may initiate post-grant review if sufficient grounds exist. The Director shall notify parties in writing within 60 days and any such determination to institute or deny is not reviewable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the Director final, nonappealable authority to institute post-grant review within a 60-day decision window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant proceedings — discovery and scope limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall set procedures for discovery of relevant evidence, including that such discovery shall be limited to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party in the proceeding, and procedures for obtaining such evidence shall be consistent with the purpose and nature of the proceeding. Regulations shall provide for discovery upon order of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constrains discovery to be proportional and focused on directly related factual assertions, with the Director controlling discovery orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant final determination timing and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall require that the final determination in a post-grant proceeding issue not later than one year after institution, except that for good cause shown the Director may extend the 1-year period by not more than six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an expedited statutory timeline for final decisions with a single short extension for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, protective orders, and sanctions in post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall provide for publication of notice in the Federal Register and on the PTO website of the filing of a petition for post-grant review and related documents, allow filings under seal exempt from publication, may provide for protective orders governing confidential information, and shall prescribe sanctions for abuse of discovery, process, or other improper use designed to harass or cause unnecessary delay or cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances transparency (publication) with confidentiality (protective orders) and authorizes sanctions to prevent abusive litigation tactics in post-grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for prescribing post-grant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing regulations the Director shall consider the effect on the economy, the integrity of the patent system, and the efficient administration of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs PTO to weigh systemic and policy impacts when designing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response in post-grant review — evidence and expert opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: After institution, the patent owner shall have the right to file, within a time period set by the Director, a response to the cancellation petition and shall file with the response, through affidavits or declarations, any additional factual evidence and expert opinions relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires patent owner to present factual evidence and experts within Director-established deadlines to defend against cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards in post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumption of validity set forth in section 282 shall not apply in a challenge under this chapter. The party advancing a proposition shall have the burden of proving that proposition by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lowers the burden and removes statutory presumption of validity in post-grant review compared to district-court litigation standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of patent during post-grant review — scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to a challenge, the patent owner may file one motion to amend to cancel any challenged claim, propose substitute claims for each challenged claim, or amend drawings/other than claims. Additional motions allowed only for good cause. An amendment may not enlarge the scope of the claims or introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited amendment options but forbids broadening or adding new matter; extra amendments require good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision, effect, and issuance of certificate after post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proceeding is instituted and not dismissed, the PTAB shall issue a final written decision on patentability of any challenged claim and any new claim added. If final and appeal time expired or appeal terminated, the Director shall issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined unpatentable and incorporating any new claim determined patentable. New claims incorporated have the same effect as set forth in section 252 for reissued patents regarding prior users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies final written decision requirement, administrative certificate process, and legal effect of incorporated new claims on prior users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and filing of termination agreements in post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review shall be terminated with respect to any petitioner upon joint request of petitioner and patent owner unless PTAB issued a written decision before the request; any agreement or understanding in connection with termination must be in writing and filed in the Office, and may be kept separate from the file if requested and made available only to government agencies on written request or to any person on showing good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires written, filed settlement agreements to ensure transparency and potential limited confidentiality with access rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to other pending proceedings; Director control and stays
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding certain statutes, the Director may determine how any reexamination, reissue, interference, derivation, or post-grant review pending during a post-grant review may proceed, including stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination. The Director may stay a post-grant review if a pending civil action for infringement addresses the same or substantially the same questions of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the Director broad case-management authority to coordinate administrative proceedings and avoid duplicative/conflicting adjudications with district court litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of civil action decisions on post-grant review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final decision in a civil action establishes that a party has not sustained its burden of proving invalidity of any patent claim, that party and its privies may not thereafter request a post-grant review on that patent claim on grounds that the party raised or could have raised; and the Director may not maintain a post-grant review requested earlier by that party on such grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes estoppel on parties who lost on invalidity grounds in district court to pursue the same grounds later in administrative post-grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of final favorable post-grant decision on petitioner's future actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final decision under section 330 is favorable to patentability of any original or new claim challenged, the cancellation petitioner may not thereafter, based on any ground the petitioner raised during the proceeding, request or pursue reexamination, derivation, post-grant review, or assert invalidity of such claim in civil actions arising under section 1338.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estops petitioners from relitigating the same invalidity grounds in administrative or judicial forums after an adverse final post-grant outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights from PTAB post-grant decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with the PTAB final determination in a post-grant proceeding may appeal the determination under sections 141 through 144 and any party to the post-grant proceeding shall have the right to be a party to the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves judicial review route for PTAB final decisions via appeal to the assigned court under specified sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Trial and Appeal Board composition and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be a Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) consisting of the Director, Deputy Director, Commissioner for Patents, Commissioner for Trademarks, and administrative patent judges. APJs shall be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability appointed by the Director. The PTAB shall review adverse examiner decisions on appeal, review adverse decisions in reexamination, review appeals under section 315, determine priority and patentability in derivation proceedings, and conduct post-grant opposition proceedings under chapter 32. Each appeal and derivation proceeding shall be heard by at least 3 members; the Director shall assign each post-grant review to a panel of 3 APJs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines institutional composition, qualifications of APJs, and the PTAB's scope of responsibilities and panel sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preissuance submissions by third parties — timing window
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may submit for consideration and inclusion in the record of a patent application any patent, published patent application, or other publication of potential relevance if such submission is made in writing before the earlier of (A) the date a notice of allowance is mailed, or (B) either (i) 6 months after publication of the application or (ii) the date of the first rejection under section 132 of any claim by the examiner during examination, whichever occurs later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a limited preissuance window for third-party prior art submissions bounded by allowance notice, a six-month post-publication window, or first claim rejection timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preissuance submission content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any preissuance submission must set forth a concise description of the asserted relevance of each submitted document; be accompanied by such fee as the Director may prescribe; and include a statement by the submitter affirming compliance with the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires concise relevance explanations, a fee, and a compliance statement for third-party preissuance submissions to be considered.
